newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger says NZ may be debt-free in seven years.
newsitem.headline: Bolger says NZ may be debt-free in seven years.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger wound up his election campaign on Friday by saying the country could be totally debt-free in seven years if current policies remained intact.
"We used to have a line ... blessed are the young, for they shall inherit the national debt," Bolger told members of the Public Relations Institute of New Zealand.
"It was true, but it need no longer be so, because one of the dramatic changes in New Zealand is that we are on course for a debt-free New zealand," Bolger said.
Bolger said very few governments around the world could even begin to contemplate being totally debt-free.

"Government debt as a percentage of GDP will go from 52 percent in 1990 to 13 percent by the turn of the century and I think we will get rid of that 13 percent, if we continue the polices, in three or four years after."
By doing so, New Zealand would be strongly positioned to face the challenges of the 21st century, one of those being that there would be far more older New Zealanders than there are now.
"They will move from having four workers to one person retired to having only two workers to one retired. We will not be able to afford the debt we have serviced in the past."
